title: Are some wallets followed within seconds on newly-traded tokens?
whyKL014Failed: KL-014's subjects held positions taken 354 to 9,085 hours ago, while a token's reachable signature history spans 2.5 to 33 hours. Every event lay outside the baseline's reach, so the comparison would have measured ERA -- busy windows during a token's rise against dead windows today -- and produced a large spurious effect. It was stopped before any number was computed, because the baseline was built first.

population.source: pump.fun coins?complete=true sorted by created_timestamp DESC

TRADEABILITY_GATE.verifiedBy: DexScreener, an external source we do not control
TRADEABILITY_GATE.why: GRADUATED IS NOT TRADED. Measured on this population before registering: of 180 recent graduates, 160 had some pair but only 37 cleared liq>=$5k and vol>=$5k. KL-012 v0.2 made exactly this mistake -- its 'winners' were graduates whose median market cap was $1,539, so both arms were failures and the run could only return a null.

RECENCY_GATE.why: the token's entire history must be pageable, so events and baseline occupy one reachable window. Verified before registering: 8 of 8 candidates fully reachable within 12 pages of 1,000 signatures.

subjects.definition: wallets with an early position in a qualifying token, excluding custodians by the inherited filter

custodianRule.failClosed: a wallet that cannot be profiled is excluded
custodianRule.inherited: thresholds carried unchanged from the KL-014 precursor rather than re-tuned. Re-tuning them now would be choosing them with knowledge of what they produced.

subjects.notInheritedFromKL014: the eleven KL-014 wallets do NOT carry over. Subjects are whoever appears in this fresh population, so the post-hoc selection that produced those eleven does not contaminate this run.

measure.statistic: distinct signing wallets acting on the token in the 60 seconds after a subject's first transaction on it

baseline.rule: random 60-second windows drawn from the SAME reachable history as the events, excluding any window overlapping a subject event
baseline.builtFirst: the baseline is computed before any subject event is measured. This is the only procedural change that has caught an error before it produced a number.

endpoint.H0: followers after a subject's first buy = wallets in an arbitrary window
endpoint.DIRECTION_PREDICTED: subject events are followed by MORE distinct wallets
endpoint.test: paired sign test on (followers - that token's median baseline), two-sided

effectRequires.property: every event lies inside the token's reachable history
effectRequires.rule: an event outside it is DISCARDED, not compared
effectRequires.why: the exact failure that stopped KL-014

effectRequires.property: baseline windows are not all identical per token

singleTestRule: one window length, one statistic, one test. No sweeping.
knownLimits: a transaction touching a token is not necessarily a buy; direction is not parsed, so 'follower' over-counts
pump.fun graduates under 6 hours old only
tokens are young, so 'success' is not yet observed -- this measures following behaviour, not whether following was profitable
